Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
Summary:
• 19-year-old female with 6–7 days of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic aching pain, and new pink-tinged urine.  
• No fever, flank/back pain, nausea/vomiting, or vaginal discharge.  
• Past history IBS; on combined OCP and Mebeverine; allergic to Clindamycin.  

Consistent clinical reasoning:
– Most likely acute uncomplicated cystitis (bacterial UTI) per typical symptom triad and absence of systemic signs (DDx high likelihood).  
– Alternative consideration: Chlamydial or gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis given recent unprotected intercourse, but less suggestive as no discharge or pelvic pain (DDx moderate likelihood).  
– Bladder/ureteric stone low likelihood; no colicky or flank pain.  

Plan:
1. Empiric oral antibiotic: choice offered—Nitrofurantoin 3-day course or Trimethoprim 3-day course (exact agent not documented).  
2. Provide urine pot; patient to submit mid-stream urine sample for dipstick and culture; adjust antibiotics if culture indicates resistance.  
3. Hydration advice—drink plenty of fluids.  
4. Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.  
5. Safety-net: seek review if fever, back/flank pain, vomiting, or no improvement within one week.  
6. Discussed unlikely link between single cannabis use and current symptoms; advised avoidance for general health.  
7. Pregnancy risk discussed; currently on OCP, last period 2 weeks ago—monitor if symptoms persist.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis — High likelihood: classic dysuria, frequency, suprapubic pain, microhematuria; no systemic features.  
2. Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis — Moderate likelihood: unprotected sex; could mimic cystitis but absence of discharge/pelvic pain lowers probability.  
3. Distal ureteric or bladder stone — Low likelihood: hematuria possible but lacks colicky flank pain and patient is low-risk age group.
